blocks.text: Pakistan has several raw materials that are important for its chemical industries; the feedstock of an industry decides its location and economic viability. Air provides nitrogen for fertilisers and oxygen for steel making. Water is used as a solvent, a cooling agent and a source of hydrogen. Fossil fuels such as coal, oil and natural gas provide the hydrocarbons needed for 90% of organic chemicals.

items: Natural gas: a major source of methane (CH4), used to produce fertilisers (urea) and petrochemicals; it is both a fuel and a source of hydrogen.

Rock salt (Khewra mines): Khewra has one of the world's largest rock salt deposits; it is the source of sodium chloride (NaCl), the raw material for soda ash (Na2CO3), caustic soda (NaOH) and chlorine.
Limestone: very abundant in the Salt Range and Sindh; the source of calcium carbonate (CaCO3) for the cement industry.
Gypsum: used in the cement industry and for making plaster; also a source of calcium and sulphur and a soil conditioner.
Chromite: found in Muslim Bagh; used in stainless steel and pigment production.
Crude oil: refined to produce a wide range of fuels and petrochemicals.
Sulphur: used to make sulphuric acid (H2SO4), a key industrial chemical.

blocks.title: Did you know?
blocks.text: Pakistan has abundant natural gas, the main raw material for making urea (NH2CONH2). Because the raw material is available locally, production costs are lower, which makes fertilisers more affordable for farmers.
